_readme: Template only. Copy to config.json, fill in your paths and delete the '_example' line. The main_*.py scripts refuse to run any config containing '_example'.

_dataset_video_alternative._readme: Rename to 'dataset' to evaluate one video. 'labels' can be the folder of .txt files or a CVAT/YOLO export root containing labels/<split>/ (its data.yaml is then used for class names). start_index = label number of the video's first frame (0 if labels start at frame_000000).
_dataset_video_alternative.name: my_video

_dataset_batch_alternative: To evaluate a folder of videos / frame folders against a folder of label folders, see config.batch.example.json.

cameras._readme: Calibration for main_points3d.py / main_tracks3d.py (OpenCV conventions). One entry per camera; each is paired with the batch input whose folder name contains the camera name (or its optional 'match' string). matrix = 3x3 intrinsics. distortions = k1 k2 p1 p2 k3 for model 'pinhole' (k1 k2 k3 k4 for 'fisheye'). rotation (Rodrigues vector, or a 3x3 matrix) and translation are WORLD -> CAMERA, as returned by stereoCalibrate / solvePnP; the reference camera has rotation [0, 0, 0] and translation [0, 0, 0]. translation is multiplied by t_scale (1000: calibration in metres, world in mm). image_size = [width, height] the calibration was done at (matrix is rescaled if the videos differ). frame_offset is added to that camera's frame numbers to synchronise the views.

tracking3d._readme: Pixel values are in undistorted pixels; distances in world units (cameras t x t_scale). conf_threshold null = every saved prediction. min_track_extent drops tracks that barely move (static false positives). n_tracks null = keep every track that passes min_track_frames, else keep the n with the most supporting detections. static_radius_px / static_min_fraction: before tracking, predicted detections at a spot (within static_radius_px) the detector fires on in at least static_min_fraction of a view's frames are removed as background clutter; static_min_fraction null = keep them. Keep the fraction above the share of the video a fly can sit still for.
tracking3d._evaluation_readme: main_tracks3d.py / main_tracks3d_guided.py write each run to <run>/3d/<model>/factor_graph/<tracks|guided>_<datetime>/ and, when the run has ground-truth labels, evaluate the tracks. eval_match_distance = how close (world units) a track point must be to a ground-truth 3D point to count as a match (evaluation_3d.txt). evaluate_2d = recompute the 2D metrics with the tracks projected back into each camera, a box inserted wherever a track has no detection (evaluation_2d.txt); backproj_score = the confidence given to those boxes (keep it >= the model confidence threshold, or they only count towards mAP). visualise_backproj_graph = redo the 2D track plots with the inserted boxes drawn in orange (track_plots_backproj/). visualise_backproj_video = one video per camera in reprojection/<camera>.mp4: detector boxes in blue, ground truth in green, every track's reprojected position as a red dot in every frame (also on top of detector boxes, to show how well the track follows them), inserted boxes in red (H.264 through ffmpeg if installed, else larger mp4v files). With either of the two, the inserted boxes are also saved as YOLO labels like the run's predictions: reprojection/labels/<input>/<sequence>/<frame>.txt (class xc yc w h score) plus data.yaml.
tracking3d._guided_readme: main_tracks3d_guided.py only. anchor_pixel_sigma = trust in a hand-placed start/end point (px). A start / end is seeded by the unguided track (else tracklet) passing within anchor_gate_px of its annotation, or starting / ending up to anchor_frame_window frames away, allowing anchor_max_px_per_frame of movement per frame in between. guided_iterations = association / optimisation rounds per object.

arena_plotting._readme: Static arena objects (fruit, leaves, arena frame) drawn into the 3D plots and the reprojection images of main_points3d.py / main_tracks3d.py / main_tracks3d_guided.py (--no-arena to skip). fruit: the red fake fruit, found without annotations. hsv: per view, the median of 'frames' frames spread over the video is thresholded in HSV (OpenCV hue 0-179; red wraps around 0, hence two hue_ranges; min_saturation keeps out the pink walls, min_value the soil), opened (open_px) and closed (close_px), and round blobs (area >= min_area_px, area / enclosing circle >= min_fill) become candidates, largest max_candidates first. mesh: the combination of one candidate per view that triangulates with every reprojection error <= max_reprojection_px is the fruit (most views first). It is drawn as a lit 'shape' ('hemisphere', as in caliscope, or 'cylinder') standing 'depth' off the wall along 'normal'; null = radius measured from the blobs, depth = radius, normal = towards the mean camera centre (world units, as cameras.t_scale). The result is cached in <run>/3d/fruit/fruit.json, with each view's mask and candidates in <run>/3d/fruit/hsv/<camera>.jpg - check these if the fruit looks wrong.

leaves._readme: The green tape star around the fruit, drawn flat on the fruit's wall (needs the fruit). hsv: per view, the fruit's median frame is thresholded for green (hue_range, OpenCV 0-179; min_saturation, min_value), opened (open_px) and closed (close_px); the outer contour containing the fruit's reprojected centre (or within max_fruit_gap_px of it) is the leaves' outline. mesh: each view's outline is laid onto the wall plane (camera rays hit the plane through the fruit's base, normal = fruit normal), filled on a raster of 'resolution' within max_extent of the fruit (world units), and kept where >= min_views views agree. The terminal reports each view's IoU with the result (close to 1 = calibration and wall plane agree). Cached in <run>/3d/leaves/, masks in <run>/3d/leaves/hsv/<camera>.jpg.

arena._readme: The arena frame (a tapered box of pipes), grown out from the fruit by its measured size: no segmentation. Its back face lies on the fruit's wall, upright (the cameras' image-up direction), with the fruit fruit_height above its bottom edge and fruit_across right of its centre line; the front face is front_size, 'depth' out of the wall, on the same centre line; the bottom edges are the floor. Sizes are [width, height] between pipe centres, in world units. depth is measured from the fabric back wall the fruit is stuck to, so it is longer than the pipe-to-pipe 150 (170 fits the images of run_20261008-101724_showoff_1). It is only as good as the fruit's placement on the back wall: check the dashed frame in the reprojection images.
